newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Nationwide Insurance eyes acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Nationwide Insurance eyes acquisitions.

text.p: Nationwide Insurance Enterprise is on the prowl for possible acquisitions in any of its three core businesses, where a string of blockbuster deals in the past year have intensified competitive pressures.
"It's only within the last year that we have concluded that we may need to do some acquisitions," Nationwide Chief Executive Dimon Richard McFerson said in a recent interview.
McFerson declined to identify a particular sector as an area the company was most interested in targeting.
"We're still in the infancy of all of that, as to where would be the best place for us in the acquisition marketplace," he told Reuters earlier this week.
To be sure, the Columbus, Ohio-based insurer will stick to its three main businesses -- personal and commercial property insurance as well as life insurance.

Nationwide is the fourth-largest auto insurer in the United States, the sixth-largest homeowners' insurer. Its Nationwide Financial Services Inc subsidiary is the country's 14th-largest life insurer in terms of assets.
Nationwide also offers commercial property insurance through its Wausau Insurance Cos unit.
"We view ourselves as an important player; we're a very large player," he said.

"We want to continue to be viewed as an important, large player in the future, and so we cannot ignore the acquisition activity and may need to do some ourselves to protect our positions in the market," he said.

Just this week, the Dutch financial services company Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV agreed to acquire Equitable of Iowa Cos for $2.2 billion, substantially strengthening its position in the U.S. life and annuity market.
General Electric Co's GE Capital late last month agreed to acquire Leucadia National Corp's Colonial Penn P&C Group, a direct marketer of auto insurance, for almost $1 billion.
And General Motors Corp's General Motors Acceptance Corp last month agreed to acquire non-standard auto insurer Integon Corp in a deal valued at $550 million.
Those deals came on top of SAFECO Corp's agreement last month to acquire commercial property-casualty insurer American States Financial Corp from Lincoln National Corp for about $2.8 billion.
McFerson declined comment on speculation that Nationwide, a mutual insurance company, had been one of the parties interested in acquiring American States.
Although Lincoln National sold its property-casualty business to focus on life insurance, Nationwide has no plans to follow suit.

"We have major positions in property-casualty and major positions in life and financial products, so for us to say we'll exit one to concentrate on the other --- we're going to concentrate on both of those areas," he said.
Still, the company is working to exit non-core businesses. "We're trying to get ourselves positioned so we're focusing on our core businesses," he said.
Nationwide earlier this year agreed to sell its West Coast Life Insurance Co subsidiary.
He declined to say which other businesses Nationwide may still seek to exit.
